paper_title: Investigating the gamma-ray burst from decaying MeV-scale axion-like particles produced in supernova explosions
suggested_experiment_name: SN1987A gamma-ray burst (SMM) - decaying ALPs with photon coalescence
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on the y-axis
notes: Paper presents an updated SN 1987A gamma-ray decay bound on MeV-scale ALP-photon coupling (SMM non-observation), newly including photon coalescence production which extends the excluded mass range up to ~280 MeV (previously ~200 MeV). No numerical table of the exclusion contour is provided; data points are inferred from text: case 1 (ma=1 MeV, g=1e-11 GeV^-1) is described as 'close to the maximal allowed value', and case 2 (ma=100 MeV, g=4e-13 GeV^-1) as 'a factor ~5 below the maximal allowed value', implying the bound is ~1e-11 GeV^-1 at 1 MeV and ~2e-12 GeV^-1 at 100 MeV. Bound applies for masses roughly 30 keV to 280 MeV. Exclusion is quoted at both 2-sigma and 3-sigma levels for SMM. The paper ALSO contains a Fermi-LAT sensitivity PROJECTION for a future nearby SN reaching g~1e-13 GeV^-1 (95% CL), but the primary new measured result is the SN1987A bound reported here. Not a DM haloscope; no local DM density assumption.
